images.title: Take the taller stack
images.purpose: Show the LCM of 96 and 360 built by taking, for each prime, the larger number of occurrences.
images.composition: Three pairs of stacked square columns stand on one baseline in the centre, the taller stack of each pair outlined, with a small key above and one result line below; open white space.
exact_structure: Key line above: a teal #0072B2 square with the text 96 and an amber #E69F00 square with the text 360.
One grey #6B7280 baseline with three groups, labelled under the baseline 2s, 3s and 5s from left to right.
Group 2s: a teal stack of exactly 5 squares beside an amber stack of exactly 3 squares.
Group 3s: a teal stack of exactly 1 square beside an amber stack of exactly 2 squares.
Group 5s: no teal squares at all, the baseline left bare in the teal position with no outline or placeholder, beside an amber stack of exactly 1 square.
In each group the taller stack (teal 5 in 2s, amber 2 in 3s, amber 1 in 5s) has a thick reddish purple #CC79A7 outline around it; exactly 3 outlined stacks.
rejection: any teal square above the 5s label
square counts other than teal 5, 1, 0 and amber 3, 2, 1
an outline on the shorter stack of any group, or an LCM other than 1440
images.takeaway: For the LCM, take each prime as many times as it occurs in whichever number has the most of it.
images.description: Stacks of squares for the 2s, 3s and 5s of 96 and 360, with the taller stack of each outlined, giving LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 1440.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on taking the maximum occurrences of each prime for 96 and 360.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two stacks in each group and keep the taller one; a missing prime counts as an empty stack.

image_decisions.why: Paired stacks make the maximum count rule easy to see at a glance.
